maya: Anyone else hitting 'TypeError: unsupported operand' in eval-runner when loading a quantized FP16 model locally? CLI exits with code 1. Repro: `ri-eval run --config evals/quantize/galen.yaml --model outputs/galen-q4f16`

arjun: I saw this earlier. Looks like the metric pipeline expects float32 tensors, and the quantized loader yields fp16. Quick hack is to cast in the runner, but that feels brittle.

liz: CI is reproducing it in nightly-evals too — failing job here: https://ci.internal/redwood/nightly-evals/4232 :confused: We should fail fast on bad configs (quantize: true + dtype: fp16 mismatch).

ci-bot: CI failed: nightly-evals/2024-04-20 03:21Z — exit code 1. Logs: runner.py:237 TypeError at metrics.compute -> see attached.

maya: Minimal traceback pasted: `File "runner.py", line 237, in _collect
    return np.mean(scores).astype(np.float32)
TypeError: can't convert sequence of sequences to float`

arjun: Root cause I think: our BLEU scorer returns a list per hypothesis when beam_size > 1, but the metric aggregator expects a scalar per sample. So aggregation tries to take mean over nested lists. Two paths: 1) change scorer to always return scalar (e.g., choose best beam) or 2) beef up aggregator and config to explicitly state per_example shape.

liz: I prefer adding explicit metric schema and a config validator. Also we should add a `ri-eval validate-config` CLI subcommand to run quick checks before executing a full eval.

jamie: I'll draft a tiny RFC: - add metric contract fields: `return_type: scalar|list`, `per_item_shape`, - implement pydantic validation for eval configs, - add `--dry-run` / `--quick-check` flags to CLI that run 10 samples and validate shapes/load.

arjun: For CI wiring: nightly-evals job should run `ri-eval validate-config` as a gating step. Also add a smoke load step that tries to import the quantized model binary and runs a single forward to catch loader/dtype issues early.

maya: I'll put together a patch with tests. Plan: (1) add pydantic metric schema + tests for BLEU scorer with beam outputs, (2) dtype compatibility checks between model and metric, (3) CLI `validate-config` + docs, (4) CI change to run validator and smoke load. ETA: tomorrow morning. cc @liz

liz: SGTM. Please also surface validation failures in the reporting dashboard (per-run validation section) so oncall can triage flaky evals quickly. :thumbsup:
